title: IPO Report Card: 30 to 60 Days After Listing — November 2026
description: Out of 66 IPOs that listed 30 to 60 days ago, 24 are currently trading above their original IPO price. 42 companies are currently trading below their IPO pric.

faq.a: An IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a private company first offers its shares to the public, allowing ordinary people to buy a part of the company.

faq.q: How do I apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your demat account provider (broker) using ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) or UPI.

"Allotment" is the process where shares are distributed to applicants who successfully bid for them in an IPO. Due to high demand, you might not get all the shares you applied for, or sometimes none at all.
SME IPOs are for Small and Medium Enterprises that list on dedicated platforms (like NSE Emerge or BSE SME) for smaller companies, often with different listing rules than larger Mainboard IPOs.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies and list on the main exchanges (NSE and BSE), while SME IPOs are for smaller companies and list on special SME platforms with different market capitalisation and trading volume requirements.
